subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: I know the parts of a good review.
I can use adjectives and adverbs in a review.
I can plan, write and check my own review of an app or game.

tf.s: A review should start with a short introduction.
tf.why: An introduction tells the reader what the review is about.

tf.s: A good review gives good points and bad points.

tf.why: They are adverbs; they tell us how something happens.
They describe a noun, like a brilliant app.

tf.s: Reviews often use “you”, for example “You can upload photos easily.”
tf.why: Using you speaks directly to the reader.

tf.s: The FunTimeforKids app opens very quickly.
tf.why: It takes two minutes to open, which is too slow.

tf.s: A good point about FunTimeforKids is its tools for painting and drawing.
tf.why: Yes, those tools are one of its good points.

tf.s: “It opens more quickly than the old app” uses a comparative adverb.
tf.why: More quickly than compares how two things work.

tf.s: A review must not say anything bad about the app.
tf.why: Honest reviews include bad points too.

tf.s: After you write your review, you should never change anything.
tf.why: Checking with a checklist and rewriting a sentence makes your review better.

boxes.q: How long does FunTimeforKids take to open?
boxes.why: The review says it takes two minutes to open.
Easily tells us how; many adverbs end in -ly.

boxes.q: Turn the note “upload photos – easy” into a sentence.
boxes.why: We use the adverb easily after the verb.

boxes.q: What is a bad point about FunTimeforKids?
boxes.why: Opening slowly is a problem, so it is a bad point.

boxes.q: Complete: It opens more ___ than the old app.
What comes at the end of a review?
boxes.why: A conclusion gives your final opinion.

boxes.q: Which sentence talks to the reader?
o: It helps you learn new words.
boxes.why: It helps you … speaks directly to the reader.

boxes.q: Which word fits a bad point?
boxes.why: Expensive means it costs a lot, which is a bad point.

boxes.q: Complete: It works ___ on my old phone.
boxes.why: Works is a verb, so we use the adverb slowly.

hunt.q: Opens too slowly is a ___ point.

mcq.q: What does an adverb do in a review?
o: It tells us how something happens.
mcq.why: Adverbs like easily and slowly describe how.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a usual part of a review?
mcq.why: A review has an introduction, good points and bad points.

mcq.q: Which adjectives are in the TechWhizz review?
mcq.why: Great and fantastic are adjectives from the review.

mcq.q: Which is a good introduction sentence for a review?
o: This is a great app for children who like learning languages.
mcq.why: An introduction says what the app is and who it is for.

o: You can learn new words quickly.
You can learn new words quick.
You can quickly new words learn.
You can learning new words quickly.
mcq.why: can + verb, then the adverb quickly.

mcq.q: Note: “print – cheap”. Which sentence is correct?
mcq.why: We use the adverb cheaply after the verb and its object.

mcq.q: Which sentence is a bad point?
o: It works slowly on my old phone.
mcq.why: Working slowly is a problem for the user.

o: To speak directly to the reader and show how the app helps them.
Because the writer forgot their name.
To ask the reader a question.
mcq.why: You makes the reader imagine using the app.

mcq.q: A review says only: “It’s brilliant! It’s fantastic!” What is missing?
mcq.why: A useful review also gives details and bad points.

o: This app opens more quickly than my old app.
mcq.why: More quickly than compares two things.
